description:
## Problem

`run_osd_campaign` drives its per-block evaluator through a sequential `FnMut(OsdBlockContext<'_>) -> OsdBlockOutcome` loop, so `ebch_osd_awgn_campaign` runs one thread (observed: `Threads: 1`, 99.7% of one core on a 24-thread host during the 2026-08-27 rigorous campaign). The crate ships rayon and a parallel executor stack that the other campaign binaries (`dvb_t2_awgn_campaign`, `ldpc_bler_sweep`) already use; the OSD tool predates none of it. The dominant grid cell (order-2, 5.23 dB, ~4e7 blocks) pays the full cost.

Statistical correctness is unaffected; this is throughput only.

## Fix sketch

Converge on the crate's deterministic-parallelism convention (convention-convergence) instead of a bespoke mechanism: `gf2_sim::parallel` (design doc §3, §11) already provides the per-worker ChaCha20 word-position seek (`worker_offset`), per-worker contexts and counters (`WorkerCtx`), and fixed-order reduction, with byte-identical results across worker counts for a fixed seed. Blocks carry global indices independent of the executing worker, so the stopping rule becomes index-ordered truncation: a cell completes at the smallest block index whose in-order cumulative block-error count reaches K, and blocks evaluated speculatively past that index contribute to no counter. The evaluator contract moves off `FnMut` to per-worker evaluators; the campaign binary adapts.

Adopting worker-seeked streams changes the sampled block sequence relative to the retired serial binary; that is a new behavioral identity recorded in provenance as usual. The identity contract becomes worker-count invariance, with the single-worker run as the reference.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The protocol evaluates blocks on multiple threads while committing outcomes in block-index order; for a fixed campaign and seed, all counters, the stopping index, and every `cell_results` entry are byte-identical across worker counts (single-worker run as reference), demonstrated at least for {1, 2, 8, 24}. The receipt differs across worker counts only in the invocation provenance REQ-04 requires.
- [hard] REQ-02: The stopping design is preserved structurally: completion exactly at the block carrying the K-th block error; speculative blocks beyond it contribute to no counter.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test compares multi-worker and single-worker runs of a scripted evaluator and asserts identical results; existing resume and protocol tests pass, with byte-identity fixtures re-pinned to the new behavioral identity where the stream change requires it.
- [hard] REQ-04: Worker count defaults to available parallelism, is settable via a CLI flag, and appears in the receipt's invocation argv provenance.
- [hard] REQ-05: Measured speedup on an order-2 probe cell on the 24-thread host is reported in the issue closure notes.
- [hard] REQ-06: Parallelism is driven through the existing `gf2_sim::parallel` primitives (worker-offset seek discipline, ordered reduction); any deviation is a named tracked exception cited in rustdoc and backed by a tracker issue (convention-convergence).

## Closure notes

Landed on `main` as merge `1e2d4885` (worker commit `bd329216`).

REQ-05 measurement, from the committed receipt `dev/bench_results/2026-08-27-258be082-osd-campaign-worker-scaling.md` (linked to this issue as a document): on the pinned 24-thread host, sampling a fixed 120000-block prefix of the order-2 1.55 dB cell, three trials per worker count.

| workers | mean wall clock | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 77.68 s | 1.00× |
| 2 | 40.81 s | 1.90× |
| 8 | 12.37 s | 6.28× |
| 24 | 6.27 s | 12.40× |

Throughput rises from 1545 to 19139 blocks/s. The host has 12 physical cores with 2 SMT threads each, so the 24-worker figure is 103% of linear physical-core scaling; the decode loop is compute-bound and SMT contributes the residual. All 12 trials produced byte-identical cell evidence (SHA-256 `8c95f21e2200c92cefd17717c390c69a7f34bdc74bc5ecdd81b0cb2ceac987a8`), an end-to-end witness of REQ-01 on the real evaluator alongside the in-process scripted tests.

Carrying this speedup to the campaign's dominant order-2 5.23 dB cell is an estimate, not a measurement: order-2 per-block cost is approximately independent of $E_b/N_0$ because the reprocessing candidate list is fixed by the order and code parameters, but that cell was not timed.

Second, unbudgeted win: the retired evaluator replayed the whole durable prefix when a cell was rebound on resume, costing $O(n)$ per resume and $O(n^2)$ across a campaign. The worker-offset seek makes rebinding $O(1)$.

Not measured: worker counts above the host's 24 logical threads (correct, but the excess serializes), and the `OSD_WAVE_BLOCKS_PER_WORKER = 16` wave-size constant, which changes how much speculative work a cell performs past its stopping block and never the committed result.
title: OSD campaign protocol evaluates blocks single-threaded, idling 23 of 24 host threads
